History of Present Illness:
81-year-old woman. Two days of poor intake and mild right upper abdominal discomfort without prominent vomiting. She is alert and reports that pain worsens with deep inspiration.

Physical Examination:
Localized right subcostal tenderness without generalized rigidity. Temperature 37.1 C; heart rate 100/min; BP 116/70 mmHg; respiratory rate 18/min; SpO2 97% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 14.0 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.1 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 304 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 136 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.7 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 153 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 44 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 72 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 55 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 109 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: distended gallbladder with stones, 5 mm wall and surrounding fluid; focal probe tenderness is present.
